facts.raw_span: a 12-year history of recurrent follicular lymphoma
a subacute, multifocal, pruritic, painful eruption
denied fevers, chills, weight loss, or other systemic symptoms
oxycodone, duvelisib (a PI3K inhibitor), and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
well-demarcated erythematous plaques on the abdomen, axillae, and inguinal folds
scattered erythematous scaly papules and plaques on the scalp, extremities, and hands
confluent erythematous hyperkeratotic plaques with plate-like scales on the plantar feet

parakeratosis with collections of neutrophils, hypogranulosis, regular epidermal hyperplasia with elongated rete ridges, thin suprapapillary plates, dilated papillary dermal vessels, and dermal eosinophils
findings consistent with a psoriasiform drug reaction
started 14 months earlier for lymphoma management
Two skin biopsies (abdomen and left foot)
